prompt: The supplement of an angle is $4$ times the angle's complement. Find the measure of the angle, in degrees.
hint: Call the angle $x$. Its supplement is $180 - x$ and its complement is $90 - x$.

hints.text: Call the angle $x$. Its supplement is $180 - x$ and its complement is $90 - x$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up on a number: for a $30^\circ$ angle the supplement is $150$ and the complement is $60$, so supplement $= 2.5 \times$ complement — not $4$. Write that same relationship with $x$ instead of guessing.
Translate the sentence into $180 - x = 4(90 - x)$ and distribute the 4.

explanation: Let the angle be $x$. Its supplement is $180 - x$; its complement is $90 - x$.
The sentence says supplement $= 4 \times$ complement: $180 - x = 4(90 - x)$.
Distribute: $180 - x = 360 - 4x$. Add $4x$ to both sides and subtract 180: $3x = 180$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Guess and adjust
steps: Try $x = 45$: supplement 135, complement 45, ratio $3$ — too small.
Try $x = 60$: supplement 120, complement 30, ratio exactly $4$. That is the angle.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The common wrong answer is 30 — the complement — because it is the number that shows up in the final check.
Label your variable in words before you solve: "$x =$ THE ANGLE." Then $x = 60$ is the answer, and 30 and 120 are just its complement and supplement along for the ride.
